learning.why: teacher made me explain why distance connects to freshness directly

end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels to reach us.
Compared nearby and distant foods using distance travelled.
Explained links between distance, fuel use, pollution, and freshness.
Used examples including bread, apples, spinach, chips, and strawberries.
Teach-back was not passed; some explanations were repeated with prompting.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and comparing foods from nearby and distant sources. They clearly connected longer distances with more fuel and pollution, and shorter distances with better freshness. They initially repeated the refrigeration example rather than adding a new point, but later explained that nearby food arrives sooner and stays fresh, correcting the explanation after the last time it was seen. At home, compare two foods and discuss which travelled farther and what that might mean for fuel, pollution, and freshness.
